title: Share or keep?

slides.title: Public or private?
slides.text: Public gets you seen and found. Private keeps you safe. A good choice names the tradeoff.

slides.title: Tricks start with public facts
slides.text: Most tricks start with facts that are already public: a name, a school, a daily route. Fooling people into giving away more is social engineering.

slides.title: Post your art?
slides.text: Weigh both sides before you make something public.
steps: risk: a school logo in the photo shows where you are

slides.title: Build on others' work
slides.text: Real programs reuse other people's code, art and sound. The license says what you may do. Attribution is credit written the way the license asks.

slides.title: Your footprint
slides.text: Everything you post adds to your digital footprint. Before you post, ask: what could someone do with this?

everything about you that can be found online

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Write the credit line for a game that reuses a template, some art and a free sound. Then name one thing you keep private online and the tradeoff of keeping it private.

talk: Why share anything at all? What is worth the risk?
